commits.message: test(e2e): serve a production build via Playwright webServer + retries
commits.message_full:
test(e2e): serve a production build via Playwright webServer + retries

The e2e suite previously required a hand-started `next dev --turbo`
server. Under sustained load that dev server's Turbopack worker pool
crashes (EPIPE / "Jest worker exceeding retry limit"), returning 500s on
/api/** that surfaced as flaky auth failures (e.g. change-password and
reset-password re-login).

Add a Playwright webServer that builds and serves a compiled production
app (`pnpm build && pnpm start`), which has no dev-worker pool and is both
stable and much faster. Locally an already-running server is reused; CI
builds fresh. Add retries (CI 2 / local 1) as a flaky safety net.

`next start` is unsupported with `output: standalone`, so gate the
standalone output behind E2E_DISABLE_STANDALONE, which the webServer sets
alongside DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRATEGY=database_url_first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: fix(settings): drop nested <main>; harden settings e2e asserts
commits.message_full:
fix(settings): drop nested <main>; harden settings e2e asserts

The settings layout rendered a <main> inside the app shell's <main>
(invalid nested landmark). Use a plain container so there is a single
<main> per page.

During streaming SSR a hidden buffer copy of a settings page can briefly
coexist with the rendered one, so getByTestId(...).toBeVisible() hit a
Playwright strict-mode violation (2 matches). Scope the settings-page
assertions to the visible instance, and assert the change-password
success via the locale-independent sonner success toast instead of a
hardcoded English string.

commits.message: fix(newsletter): fix reflected XSS and forgeable unsubscribe tokens
commits.message_full:
fix(newsletter): fix reflected XSS and forgeable unsubscribe tokens

The unsubscribe page interpolated the decrypted email straight into HTML
via c.html(), and the token used XOR with a hardcoded key, so an
attacker could forge a token carrying an XSS payload and execute script
on the app origin.

Escape the email before rendering, and replace the XOR scheme with
HMAC-SHA256 signed tokens (Web Crypto; runs on Node and Workers) keyed
by NEWSLETTER_TOKEN_SECRET (falling back to BETTER_AUTH_SECRET) with a
constant-time comparison. Add email-crypto and route XSS tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: fix(billing): require webhook secret in production for Creem and Stripe
commits.message_full:
fix(billing): require webhook secret in production for Creem and Stripe

Creem and Stripe getGatewayEvent verified the signature only when a
webhook secret was configured, falling back to JSON.parse on an
unverified body otherwise. Combined with the public notify route, an
unset (optional) secret let forged "purchase succeeded" events mint
ACTIVE billing contracts for any referenceId -- a payment bypass.

Mirror the existing Dodo guard: throw when NODE_ENV is production and no
secret is set. Add gateway security tests for the production guard,
signature mismatch, and the signed-acceptance path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
